# #201 — Expose get_entry in public Open Brain contract for Hermes exact source recall

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy

## Problem

Hermes now has runtime support for a read-only `get_entry` tool surface, but Nagatha cannot use it because hosted Open Brain `get_contract` does not advertise `get_entry` in `tool_contracts`.

Observed from Nagatha on 2026-06-25:

```text
contract_version 2026-06-19.memory-tools.v5
has_get_entry False
tool_count 11
```

Raw `mcp2cli open-brain get_entry` can read the needed session row, but contract-driven clients correctly hide tools that are not in the public contract manifest.

## Why it matters

Nagatha source-type canary currently proves exact source identity only through a noisier path. rtech-hermes PR #188 added safe provider support for contract-advertised `get_entry`, scoped to the provider/auth namespace, so exact UUID/source-type checks can avoid search/qmd fallback behavior once Open Brain exposes the tool.

## Requested fix

- Add `get_entry` to the public `get_contract` manifest capabilities/tool_contracts if it is intended to be a supported read surface.
- Ensure server-side namespace/auth predicates remain the security boundary for ID reads.
- Add/adjust contract tests so `get_entry` appears in the manifest with the expected input schema (`table`, `id`, optional namespace only if server policy allows it).
- Include downstream rollout note for Hermes: after deploy, Nagatha must refresh provider contract cache/restart and rerun the source-type canary.

## Downstream dependency

rtech-hermes PR #188 is merged and collab is pulled. It is forward-compatible only until this Open Brain contract change is live.

## Acceptance

- Hosted `mcp2cli open-brain get_contract --params "{}"` returns `tool_contracts.get_entry`.
- Nagatha provider cache refresh sees `get_entry`.
- Nagatha source-type canary can use `get_entry(table=sessions, id=...)` as a contract-native fetch path.
